Definition: from a presumed derivative of G4130; a filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification:--satisfying.
BiblicalUsage: Plesmone is a filling up, indulging the flesh. Paul uses it once, in Colossians 2:23: self-imposed worship and humility have a show of wisdom, but they are not of any value against the indulgence of the flesh.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe man-made religion feeds the flesh it pretends to starve.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
